summary: Ben Slimane Airport is a small airfield located in the Casablanca-Settat region of Morocco, roughly midway between the country's two largest cities, Casablanca and Rabat. The facility is primarily associated with the Royal Moroccan Air Force and serves limited civilian or general aviation traffic. Its compact size and strategic central location along Morocco's Atlantic corridor make it a recognizable landmark in the region.
faqs:
Q: Where is Ben Slimane Airport located?
A: It is situated in the city of Ben Slimane, Morocco, approximately between Casablanca and Rabat in the Casablanca-Settat region.

Q: Is Ben Slimane Airport open to commercial passenger flights?
A: It is primarily a military airfield associated with the Royal Moroccan Air Force, with very limited or no scheduled commercial passenger service.

Q: How far is the airport from Casablanca?
A: Ben Slimane lies roughly 40-50 km south of Casablanca, typically around a 45-minute to one-hour drive depending on traffic.

Q: Are there other airports nearby?
A: Yes, Mohammed V International Airport in Casablanca and Rabat-Salé Airport are both within about an hour's drive.
transport_tips: Taxis and private car hires are the most practical ways to reach the airport, as there is no dedicated rail station at the site. Travelers coming from Casablanca or Rabat should allow extra time, as traffic on the A1 motorway can be unpredictable during peak hours. Pre-arranging transport is recommended since on-demand service in Ben Slimane itself can be limited.
local_tip: Since the airport is small and primarily military, frequent visitors recommend confirming access and clearance in advance through official channels, and carrying identification at all times when approaching the perimeter, as security protocols are strict.
